note: PLAA deficiency features progressive cerebral atrophy, white matter abnormalities, and cerebellar vermis atrophy rather than primary pontine flattening typical of classic PCH.

evidence.text: In a patient with NDMSBA due to PLAA mutation, brain MRI showed severe white matter signal abnormalities, thinning of the corpus callosum, polymicrogyria, and severe vermis atrophy.

source.title: New Imaging and Clinical Manifestations of NDMSBA Disorder Caused by a Novel Homozygous Missense Variant of PLAA
source.quote: The brain magnetic resonance imaging revealed lissencephaly, polymicrogyria, severe subcortical, deep and deep white matter signal abnormalities, thinning of the corpus callosum, and severe vermis atrophy.

evidence.text: Pontocerebellar hypoplasia subtypes share core characteristics of hypoplasia/atrophy of the cerebellum and pons with progressive microcephaly and variable supratentorial involvement.

source.title: Classification, diagnosis and potential mechanisms in pontocerebellar hypoplasia
source.quote: All subtypes share common characteristics, including hypoplasia/atrophy of cerebellum and pons, progressive microcephaly, and variable cerebral involvement.
